title: Elastic admission controller with regional affinity and model-variant degradation
creator: Sanjay Patel
description:
Problem: We need a predictable, quota-aware admission layer that enforces plan-level priorities (free / paid / enterprise), prefers region-affine capacity, and degrades requests gracefully to cheaper model variants when capacity or quota constraints demand it. Existing admission logic is: simple token check -> fifo queue -> global throttle. That leads to noisy neighbor effects across regions, surprising preemptions for enterprise customers in multi-region outages, and poor UX for free/paid users when we perform blunt global throttles.

Goals:
- Enforce per-tenant and per-plan quotas while maximizing fairness and SLO attainment for higher tiers.
- Prefer routing to same-region pool if available (regional affinity) to reduce cross-region latency and egress cost.
- Support model-variant degradation path: request-level fallback families (high-quality -> medium-cost -> low-cost) with semantic degradation awareness.
- Provide observability hooks (admission reason, scored decision, fallback chosen) surfaced in Console and logs for debugging and RCA.

Core design (high level):
1) Admission Score Calculator: compute a 0..100 score for each incoming request from factors: plan-priority-weight (enterprise>paid>free), tenant-remaining-credit ratio, request-slo-weight (explicit latency hint), region-affinity-score (based on lastX requests and regional capacity), and model-cost-score (tokens * model-cost-estimate).
2) Leaky-Token Per-Plan Reservoirs: each plan has a soft reservoir and a hard reservoir. Soft reservoir allows temporary burst consumption up to X% above committed capacity with decay; hard reservoir enforces absolute circuit-break. Reservoirs are replenished periodically by billing/credits listeners.
3) Elastic Admission Gates: requests are admitted to one of 4 lanes: instant (score>80, map to fast pools), paced (60-80), soft-degrade (40-60, eligible for cheaper variants), and reject (<=40). Admission gates consider regional pool availability; if same-region capacity is below threshold for the chosen lane, attempt cross-region route if latency delta < configured tolerance, otherwise move request to next lower lane (soft-degrade) and select fallback variant.
4) Model-Variant Mapping: every model in catalog has a variant family defined (e.g., rwd-llama-inc -> rwd-llama-quantized -> rwd-gpt-compact). The admission controller consults family to pick candidate fallback that meets the lane's cost/latency target. There is also an allowlist/denylist by tenant for variants (enterprise customers can opt out).
5) Graceful downgrade policy: when promoting to lower lane, annotate response with reason: {admission_reason, chosen_variant, estimated_quality_delta}. Console will show degradation events per-tenant and per-route.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict priority preemption vs. bandwidth-smoothing: We choose soft-reservoirs + score-based admission to avoid oscillation and preserve baseline for lower tiers instead of instantly preempting all free requests when an enterprise spike occurs.
- Cross-region routing: favor same-region but allow cross-region within a latency budget; aggressive cross-region routing improves utilization but increases egress cost and unexpected latency. Default policy is conservative (prefer same-region), opt-in aggressive mode for customers that specifically allow cross-region failover.
- Variant fidelity vs. consistency: If fallback variant has different tokenization or structured output, we may introduce functional incompatibilities. We will only fallback to variants that pass a compatibility matrix for route types (chat vs structured output). Non-compatible fallbacks are excluded.

Acceptance criteria (for rollout to staging):
- Admission decision recorded in 100% of requests and retrievable in Console traces.
- Under synthetic overload (30% above baseline), enterprise P95 latency stays within SLO with at most 2x increase in free-tier rejection rate vs baseline.
- Fallback selection must reduce average cost/token by >= 35% for soft-degrade lane in tests.
- E2E tests that validate region-affinity respects configured latency budget and that opt-out flags for variants work per-tenant.

Implementation plan and phasing:
Phase 1 (design + infra): schema for admission events, repo for admission service, model-family registry extension, metrics + traces. (Owner: Ava, Infra: Diego)
Phase 2 (local sim & e2e): simulator that replays traffic for multiple tenants across regions to tune scoring constants; e2e test harness with canary traffic. (Owner: Ava)
Phase 3 (staging rollout): enable policy for <10% of traffic, verify metrics and Console visibility.
Phase 4 (gradual ramp): bump to 50% then 100% after 2 weeks of no regressions.

Observability and KPIs:
- per-request fields: admission_lane, score_components, chosen_variant, region_routed, admission_latency_ms.
- KPIs: enterprise_p95_latency, paid_p95_latency, free_rejection_rate, fallback_rate, cost_per_1k_tokens_by_lane.

Backward compatibility and safety knobs:
- global feature flag: admission_v2_enabled (per-org override).
- emergency fallback: force-stop cross-region and variant fallback to put all requests through vanilla queues.
- opt-out: tenant-level variant_opt_out list stored in tenant config.
